title: Zond scan comparison
description: What changed between two zond scan reports. Version 1, counted apart from the report schema's version. Every change is one scalar fact - `{kind, before, after}` - so a set that gained two members produces two changes rather than one carrying a list. Every host and endpoint carries `confirmed`, which says whether the scan lacking a record is known to have looked at all; a consumer that ignores it will report hosts as gone every time somebody narrows a scan. Timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC. Unknown fields may appear and must be ignored.

schema_version.description: The version of this document's shape. Counted apart from the report schema's, because the two answer different questions.

engine.description: Which build wrote the document. Not which produced either scan, for which see `baseline` and `current`.

unchanged.description: Whether the two scans describe the same network. Derivable from an empty `hosts`, and stated because it is the first question every consumer asks.

hosts.description: Every host that differs, ascending by address. Hosts that did not are not here.

provenance.description: Which scan one side of the comparison was.

engine_version.description: The engine that produced the report, as it attributed itself. A report built from another tool's output says so - `nmap 7.94` and not this engine.

at.description: The moment the scan is judged to have happened, and the moment its certificates were judged against.

hosts.description: How many hosts the report held.

kinds.description: Which phases the report recorded, in the order they ran. Empty for a report carrying none.

states_scope.description: Whether the report says what it covered. False makes every coverage answer about this side `unstated`, so nothing appearing or disappearing against it can be confirmed.

confirmed.description: A count, and how much of it the other scan is known to have looked for. A consumer that alerts on one of these numbers should alert on `confirmed`: `total` includes records the other scan never covered, which are findings about the scan rather than about the network.

total.description: How many, whatever the other scan covered.

confirmed.description: How many the other scan is known to have covered.

summary.description: Counts over the whole comparison, derived from the host deltas.

certificates_expiring.description: Endpoints whose certificate is now inside the expiry threshold and was not when the earlier scan ran.

host_delta.description: One host, as the two scans between them hold it.

address.description: The address the host is reported under: the later scan's primary where it has a record, the earlier scan's where it does not.

coverage.description: What the scan lacking a record says about having covered the target. Null when both hold one, where the question does not arise.

confirmed.description: Whether this is a finding about the network rather than about the scan. This is the field to alert on.

regrouped.description: Whether the two scans grouped this host's addresses differently: what one holds as a single record the other holds as several. It happens when one scan reached the link layer and the other did not. Both sides are still compared, merged.

ports.description: Every endpoint that moved, ascending by number then transport. Endpoints identical in both scans are not here.

baseline.description: The earlier scan's whole record, in the report document's schema, or null where only the later scan has one.

current.description: The later scan's whole record, or null where only the earlier scan has one.

port_delta.description: One endpoint, as the two scans between them hold it.

coverage.description: What the scan lacking a record says about having covered the target. Null when both hold one, where the question does not arise.

confirmed.description: Whether this is a finding about the network rather than about the scan. True when both scans hold a record, and when the one that does not is known to have probed the endpoint anyway. This is the field to alert on.

opened.description: Whether the endpoint accepts connections now and did not before.

closed.description: Whether it accepted connections before and does not now.

records.description: How many records each scan held for one host. `{1, 1}` ordinarily; anything else is a regrouping.

change.description: One field that moved, as one scalar fact. A set that gained two members produces two of these rather than one carrying a list, so every change has the same shape and a rule can be written against `kind` alone.

kind.description: Which field moved. `filtering_gained` and `filtering_lost` are what the filter in front of a host was shown to be doing, which only a scan that ran the comparative probe records at all. `certificate_expiring` and `certificate_expired` are the two a certificate undergoes without being replaced: nothing about it moved, a threshold was crossed between the two scans, and `after` is when it lapses. They are also reported for a certificate that replaced one, since the baseline was never shown it and it has no earlier standing to have moved from. `finding_appeared`, `finding_resolved` and `finding_reassessed` carry a finding's severity and title; the report the diff was taken over holds its evidence. A reassessment is one claim both scans make, graded differently.

before.description: What the earlier scan found, or null where it found nothing.

after.description: What the later scan found, or null where it finds nothing.
